summary: N. Veezhinathan worked in Indology and philosophy, earning a PhD from Savitribai Phule Pune University in 1964 under A. Sankaran and studying under T. M. P. Mahadevan and T. S. Srinivasa Sastri. Posts included Deccan College (1960–1963) and University of Madras (1964).

N. Venkataramanayya was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology who studied under Ferrand E. Corley. He served as Reader in Indian History at the University of Madras (attested 1957) and Deputy Director for Epigraphy for Andhra Pradesh's archaeology department.

Nadine Stchoupak worked in Indology and linguistics, studying at Saint Petersburg State University under Sergey Oldenburg and at EPHE under Alfred Foucher, Sylvain Lévi, Louis Finot, and Antoine Meillet. She held posts at Institut de Civilisation Indienne and EPHE.

Nae Ionescu was a philosopher and religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Bucharest (~1908–1912) and the universities of Göttingen (~1913–1914) and Munich (~1915–1919). He held a post at the University of Bucharest from circa 1919 to 1938.

Nagaraj Paturi works in Indology, linguistics, and religious studies. He studied at Osmania University and the University of Hyderabad under H. S. Ananthanarayana, B. Ramakrishna Reddy, and P. Ramanarasimham. He held posts at FLAME University (attested 2015–2024) and Indica Academy (attested 2025).
Nagin J. Shah is an Indology and philosophy scholar who served as Acting Director of the L.D. Institute of Indology (attested 1968), where he succeeded Dalsukh Malvania.

Nalinaksha Dutt was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He studied at Chittagong College, Presidency University, University of Calcutta (PhD ~1921), and University of London. He held posts at Judson College, University of Calcutta (~1921–1958), The Asiatic Society, and Maha Bodhi Society.

Nalini Balbir is an Indology and linguistics scholar who studied under Colette Caillat (~1976–1980). She held posts at CNRS (1982–1988), Sorbonne Nouvelle University (1988–2022), and École Pratique des Hautes Études (from 2000; Emerita 2022).

Nalini Devdas works in religious studies, philosophy, and Indology. She earned a PhD at Concordia University under Leslie C. Orr, also studying under P. D. Devanandan, C. T. Krishnamachari, S. Collins, and R. P. Hayes, and held a post at Carleton University.

Nam-lin Hur works in Japanology, religious studies, and history. He studied at the University of Tokyo and under Helen Hardacre, Fumio Tamamuro, and Martin Collcutt. He held a postdoctoral fellowship at Harvard and a professorship at the University of British Columbia (attested 2000).

Naman P. Ahuja is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He earned his doctorate from SOAS University of London and served as Professor of Indian Art and Architecture at Jawaharlal Nehru University (attested 2018).

Namgyal Rinpoche was a Buddhist and religious studies scholar. He studied at Jarvis Baptist Seminary, the University of Michigan, and under traditional teachers Sayadaw U Thila Wunta, Mahasi Sayadaw, Phra Rajasiddhimuni, and the 16th Karmapa, founding Kagyu Samye Ling and Dharma Centre.

Namio Egami was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1927–1930), later holding posts there (~1948–1967) and as Director of the Ancient Orient Museum (~1978–2002).
Namita Das is a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy who completed her PhD at Gauhati University under the doctoral supervision of Sibnath Sarma.

Namkhai Norbu was a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Derge Gonchen, Kuse Serjong Shedra, and Khamdre Shedra under various teachers. He held teaching posts at Southwest Minzu University, IsMEO, and the University of Naples (1962–1992).

Nancy E. Levine is a scholar in Tibetology and anthropology. She held posts in anthropology at the University of California, Los Angeles, attested as Associate Professor in 1998 and Professor in 2026.

Nancy G. Lin is a Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology scholar. She studied at Bryn Mawr, Columbia, UC Berkeley, and University of Chicago. Her posts include Lawrence University and the Numata Center for Buddhist Translation and Research (attested 2026).

Nancy Hatch Dupree worked in history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. She studied at Barnard College (~1945–1949) and Columbia University (~1950–1952), and later held a post at Kabul University (~2006–2017).

Nancy Hock works in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD from the University of California, Berkeley in 1987 under Joanna Gottfried Williams, Lewis Lancaster, Eugene F. Irschick, and Barend A. van Nooten, later working at the Asian Art Museum.

Nancy McCagney is a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied under Chögyam Trungpa, Ninian Smart, Gerald James Larson, William F. Powell, and Andrew Rawlinson. She held an academic post at the University of Delaware (attested 1997).
